title: From One Family, a Whole World

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham and Japheth. (Ham was the father of Canaan.) These were the three sons of Noah, and from them came the people who were scattered over the whole earth. - Gen 9:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here Scripture pauses to note something with far-reaching significance: from Noah's three sons "came the people who were scattered over the whole earth." Every nation, every people group, every human being alive today traces back to this one family stepping out of the ark. The whole diverse human race shares a common origin, a common ancestry, a common Maker.

This is a truth with enormous implications. There are not different kinds of humans, some more valuable than others. We are all one family, all descended from Noah, all made in the image of the one God. Every distinction we use to divide ourselves - nation, tribe, colour, status - fades before this deeper reality: we are kin, all branches of a single human family tree.

This is the biblical foundation for the dignity and unity of all people. Paul declared that God "made all the nations, that they should inhabit the whole earth" from one man (Acts 17:26). No group can claim superiority; no person can be despised. We are one blood, one family, one humanity under God.

And the gospel deepens this unity beautifully. In Christ, God is gathering people "from every nation, tribe, people and language" into one family of faith (Rev 7:9). The human family scattered from Noah is being drawn back together in Jesus. Today, look at every person - of every background - as your kin, made by the same God, loved by the same Saviour.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you see all people as one human family under God?
- How should the unity of humanity shape the way you treat those different from you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that all people come from one family and share one Maker. Break down the divisions in my heart, and help me see every person as my kin. Thank You that in Christ You gather people from every nation into one family.
